summary: Baileys fork pins libsignal to unpinned personal GitHub fork
details: package.json declares the `libsignal` dependency as `github:tenka-san/libsignal-node`, a bare GitHub reference to a personal user's fork with no commit SHA, tag, or version constraint. On `npm install`, npm clones the default branch's current HEAD and runs any lifecycle scripts the fetched repository declares, executing that code on the installer's machine with no integrity check. Whoever controls the `tenka-san/libsignal-node` repository can change the code at any time, and every installer of this package will run whatever is at HEAD at that moment. The upstream `@whiskeysockets/baileys` package resolves `libsignal` from the npm registry at a pinned version; substituting a mutable third-party git reference in this fork replaces a registry-integrity-checked dependency with an unpinned attacker-controllable code source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
